title: BPS psychologist charged with sexually abusing a high-school student for 19 months
summary: A psychologist at the Edward M. Kennedy Academy for Health Careers was ordered locked up today because he could not come up with $20,000 bail at his arraignment on charges he sexually abused a student at the Edward M. Kennedy Academy for Health Careers for a year and a half, the Suffolk County District Attorney's office reports. Vladimir Casseus, 36, of Norwood, was arraigned this morning in West Roxbury Municipal Court on charges of indecent assault and battery on a person 14 or older, dissemination of obscene matter to a minor, open and gross lewdness, witness intimidation, and two counts of attempting to commit a crime, the DA's office says, adding that should he make bail, he would have to wear a GPS device, stay away from everybody under 18 save his own children. According to the DA's office: The victim, now 17, reported to one of her teachers that between October 2024 and April 2026, Casseus exposed himself to her, repeatedly enticed her to commit sexual acts with him, and repeatedly tried to touch her breasts and vagina. On several occasions Casseus showed his penis to her on FaceTime. He also commented about her appearance and told her about confidential meetings with other students. The victim reported that on multiple occasions Casseus asked her to remove her clothes during counseling sessions and threatened to report her to the Boston Emergency Services Team (BEST) and the state Department of Children and Families (DCF) if she didn't touch him. The incidents occurred in Casseus's office and other teachers' offices at the school's 10 Fenwood Road and 152 Arlington Street campuses. Casseus, who according to city records, earned $147,348 last year, is a Boston native and BPS graduate, starting at the Haley School in Roslindale. He earned a master of education in school psychology at Tufts in 2016 - and then began working for BPS. His state license as a licensed educational psychologist lapsed in December, 2023, according to state records. title: They hate us cuz they ain't us, New England pie edition
summary: WBUR takes a food historian out to lunch at the Parker House , to discuss a 19th-century movement to get New Englanders to stop eating so much pie, because, of course, eating pie led to sexual deviancy and just general degeneration. John Henry Kellogg, the guy who gave us corn flakes as a cure for sex (and who spent the last 30 years of his life as a racist eugenicist ), hated our pie-eating ways. So did Rudyard Kipling, who grew disgusted during his time living in Vermont. This at a time when: A factory in Chelsea was using "600 pounds of fowl and 150 pounds of mutton every day to make pies to sell in restaurants, lunch counters and hotels."
